claims.statement: The account introduction frames an account as identity, access and preferences foundation; this does not mean all resources are accessible or prove current credentials and roles.

The GHEC managed-user branch states enterprise provisioning and management through an IdP, with different capabilities and restrictions from standard personal accounts. Standard personal-account steps cannot be assigned to managed users solely from broad metadata.
The getting-started index routes to account, profile and personal dashboard quickstart across FPT/GHES/GHEC. Navigation is not entitlement, complete review of links or authority to mutate accounts.

The signed-in personal dashboard is described as the initial page and reachable through the GitHub logo. Recent activity, top navigation repositories/teams and search-bar recent items are convenience views, not a full estate or access inventory.

The feed feature is FPT/GHEC public preview and supports event-type filters; the other branch describes Following and For you feeds, the latter also public preview. Network recommendations and user/watch relationships are not exhaustive monitoring or authorization evidence.

The home-dashboard feature is FPT/GHEC public preview requiring New Dashboard Experience enablement. It supports Copilot prompting, agent-session/log tracking and resulting PR/task management; enabling preview or triggering agents requires applicable authority and may have external effects. Session-list presence does not prove completion or remote execution.

The profile introduction describes optional discovery and highlighting work, linking tutorials, how-tos and reference. It is not a mandatory personal disclosure obligation, permission to publish, or completeness of showcased work.

Recent activity previews up to four updates from the last two weeks, limited to open issues/PRs with the listed opening, comment, reopen, review request, assignment or commit-reference relationships. This is neither full activity coverage nor proof of no older work.

Top repositories are automatically generated from commit, issue and PR interactions, can be nonowned, cannot be manually edited and drop off one year after last interaction. A top-list entry does not prove ownership or present access.

Feed updates describe followed users starring, following, creating public repos, qualifying watched issues/PRs, pushing watched commits, public forks or releases. The feed branch is cloud public preview; Following/For you networks in the alternate branch differ. Filters and recommendations must not become a security audit log.

The home-dashboard public preview requires feature opt-in and includes Copilot prompts, task assignment, issue creation and Spark start, running/past agent sessions, recent relevant PRs and issues. These mutation-capable affordances do not grant new write authority, establish every session as live or provide exhaustive task coverage.

Repository creation and forking are described as always counted contributions; issues, PRs, reviews, discussions/answers and commits count only sometimes. Count is display criteria, not a mandate to create artifacts or a complete productivity measure.

Issues, PRs and discussions must be opened in standalone nonfork repositories and graph display has an unspecified item limit. The listing of reviews and discussion answers as sometimes counted is not fully explained by this subsection's opened-item criteria; omission or exact threshold remains unresolved.

Commit eligibility requires all of linked author email, standalone nonfork repository and default or project-site gh-pages branch; GHES explicitly includes coauthor email. In addition at least one of collaboration/org membership, having forked the repository, or having opened an issue/PR there must hold. These conjunction/disjunction requirements cannot be replaced by a single email check.

Public cloud profile contributions are visible worldwide to those accessing the cloud site, while GHES visibility is other users of the instance. Publicized private contributions expose daily counts without details to viewers lacking repository access; counts are disclosure, not guaranteed anonymity or access grant.
The GHEC data-residency subsection says achievements are unavailable on ghe.com subdomains. Broad cloud achievement references cannot override this hosting distinction.
GHES coauthored commits must meet ordinary commit criteria. Rebase credits original authors and the rebasing person; this presentation is not cryptographic authorship or authority to rewrite history.

FPT/GHEC merged personal accounts do not transfer issue, PR or discussion attribution to the new account's graph. Email relinking or repository transfers cannot certify this participation history moved.

Commit event times use commit timestamp timezone; browser-created issue/PR times use browser timezone, while API-created events use specified API time/timezone. This needs reconciliation with broad UTC calendar descriptions and date-query examples rather than treating every event as one local day.

Profile commit occurrence uses author date, whereas repository occurrence uses commit date. The source describes amend, force push, rebase or other commands as date-change contexts; do not infer that every force push inherently rewrites timestamps or execute those commands for display repair.

Shared GHES contributions show counts from the past 90 days, are classified private and reveal only counts and GHES origin. GitHub Connect requests updates hourly, which is a request cadence, not proven freshness, complete history, successful synchronization or custody transfer.
